text:
Samir: FYI customer reports internal API failing to reach service endpoint in their VPC after last week's cert rotation. Getting NXDOMAIN for svc.acme.internal.
Zara: any chance split-horizon hosted zone was touched?
Samir: customer says they rotated certs and we did a small resolver rule change for the peering. It started ~09:12 UTC. Attached dig output below.
Samir: ```bash
dig +short srv svc.acme.internal @10.0.0.10
# -> (empty)
```
Kevin: can they have overlapping hosted zones? please check Route53 ownership and list-hosted-zones-by-name. Also confirm resolver rule association order.
Samir: they sent this snippet from their account: ```text
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.internal
HostedZones: [{Id: /hostedzone/Z12ABC, Name: acme.internal, Config: {PrivateZone: true}}]
```
Zara: private zone exists. next suspect is node-local DNS cache or an on-prem forwarder returning NXDOMAIN.
NetBot: cert-rotator completed rotation for tenant acme at 2024-11-07T09:10:50Z :white_check_mark:
Anita: quick triage steps: 1) curl the vpc endpoint with SNI, 2) kubectl exec into a node and clear node-local cache, 3) verify the VPC resolver rule targets.
Samir: customer curl shows TLS handshake failure when hitting IP directly, but NXDOMAIN for hostname. curl output: ```bash
$ curl -v https://svc.acme.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://svc.acme.internal/health
* TLS handshake error: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Exiting with 35
```
Kevin: TLS failure is separate, but DNS needs fixing first. Where NXDOMAIN comes from matters.
Anita: check /etc/resolv.conf inside pod. search line or ndots can cause odd query expansions.
Samir: pod resolv.conf: ```text
nameserver 10.0.0.10
search cluster.local svc.acme.internal
options ndots:5
```
Zara: ndots:5 means the resolver will try search suffixed queries; odd but shouldn't NXDOMAIN for a FQDN.
Eng-SRE: can someone capture tcpdump of port 53 on the node-local IP to see which upstream returns NXDOMAIN? also grab node-local logs (/var/log/node-cache.log).
Samir: customer tcpdump shows response from 10.0.0.2 with NXDOMAIN flag. 10.0.0.2 is their on-prem forwarder.
Kevin: that suggests their on-prem DNS returned NXDOMAIN. Did anyone temporarily delete the record during rotation?
Samir: checking Route53 change history: change C12345 deleted the SRV record at 09:11 and it was re-created at 09:20. That matches the window.
Zara: explains the flapping. Recommendations: 1) prefer Route53 inbound endpoints for authoritative answers when we own the private zone, 2) avoid deleting records during rotation, 3) reduce node-local cache TTLs or purge cache after changes.
Anita: repro/fix steps for customer: 1) aws route53 get-change --id C12345 to confirm, 2) restart node-local (sudo systemctl restart node-local-dns) on affected nodes, 3) run `dig +trace svc.acme.internal @127.0.0.1` to validate answers.
Samir: customer restarted node-local and now hostname resolves again. TLS cert mismatch is a follow-up for cert team. For DNS this case is resolved.
Kevin: filing internal follow-up: root cause = transient Route53 deletion during cert rotation + on-prem forwarder returning NXDOMAIN + node-local cache holding NXDOMAIN. Action items: add pre-checks to cert rotation playbook, avoid deleting records until after traffic drains, and document cache purge step.
Samir: adding runbook notes, will check back with customer tomorrow to confirm full recovery. :thumbsup:
